title: Concrete strength on curing time and water–cement ratio
intro: Twelve concrete cylinders were cast from mixes with water–cement (W/C) ratios from 0.40 to 0.62 and tested after 7, 14 or 28 days of curing. The compressive strength is in MPa. The cylinders cured longest happened to come from the wetter mixes, so curing time and W/C ratio move together in this sample. The model is Strength = b₀ + b₁·Curing days + b₂·W/C ratio, fitted by least squares. Read the equation, the coefficient table, R² and the residual standard error; the line for Curing days is also shown as numbers.
